clue.text: Overwhelmed by fighting, I have to surrender

indicators.note: the contraction is engulfed by the word for fighting, so it sits inside it

parts.note: fighting is war
I have contracts to I've

explanation.surface: A soldier, swamped in battle, decides to give up.
explanation.definitionFit: A waiver is the act of giving up a right or claim, a formal relinquishment.

clue.text: Create confusion by removing cover from seats

indicators.note: the cover of a word is its outside, so the first and last letters go

parts.note: saddles are seats on horses or bicycles

explanation.surface: Someone causes chaos by stripping upholstery off chairs.
explanation.definitionFit: To addle is to muddle or confuse, so it is to create confusion.

clue.text: Struggle with objective opinion

parts.note: to vie is to struggle or compete
the point of something is its aim or objective

explanation.surface: Someone finds it hard to form an unbiased view.
explanation.definitionFit: A viewpoint is a way of looking at things, a stance or perspective.

clue.text: One rambling somewhere in Italy, we're told

indicators.note: we're told means heard spoken, so the word is taken as it sounds

parts.note: Roma is the Italian name for Rome

explanation.surface: A hiker wanders through an Italian location, apparently.
explanation.walkthrough: In a non-rhotic British accent Roma and the answer sound alike.
explanation.definitionFit: A roamer is a wanderer, someone who rambles about without fixed course.

clue.text: Expectation for particular ballet's finale

parts.note: pro means in favour of, for
spec. is the short form of specific, meaning particular

indicators.note: the finale of a word is its final letter, here of ballet, the 's tying it to finale

parts.note: the last letter of ballet

explanation.surface: Someone states what they are hoping for from one ballet's closing number.
explanation.definitionFit: A prospect is a likely future event, something hoped for or anticipated.

clue.text: Have a good time using phone and Twitter recklessly

indicators.note: recklessly means wildly, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Someone enjoys themselves by using their mobile and social media without care.
explanation.definitionFit: To paint the town red is an idiom for going out and celebrating wildly, partying.

clue.text: Excessive work penned by old writer

indicators.note: penned means enclosed as in a pen, so the work word goes inside

parts.note: Jules Verne, the French novelist
to do is to work

explanation.surface: An elderly author wrote too much.
explanation.walkthrough: 'penned' tempts as a synonym of written, but here it means shut in, as an animal in a pen; the old writer is the French science-fiction novelist.
explanation.definitionFit: Overdone means taken too far or exaggerated, as with a performance or a steak cooked too long.

clue.text: Award zero stars, perhaps, to theatrical performance

parts.note: a critic giving zero stars pans a show, slating it

explanation.surface: A reviewer gives a show no stars at all.
explanation.walkthrough: A panto (pantomime) is a British family Christmas stage show with slapstick and audience participation.
explanation.definitionFit: A panto is a comic stage entertainment, a theatre show staged mainly at Christmas.

clue.text: Star — British — in Speed

indicators.note: the B is placed inside the word for speed

parts.note: celerity is swiftness or speed

explanation.surface: A British star of the film Speed.
explanation.definitionFit: A celebrity is a famous person, a star of screen, stage or sport.

clue.text: A doctor and nurse at the front of a queue for certain medication

indicators.note: the doctor and nurse come before the queue, placed ahead of it

parts.note: EN is an Enrolled Nurse in British usage
a queue is a line

explanation.surface: A doctor and nurse stand at the head of a line of patients waiting for their drugs.
explanation.definitionFit: Adrenaline is a hormone also given as a drug, for example in an injector for severe allergic reactions.

clue.text: Flower engulfed by receding shoreline

indicators.note: receding means going back, so the run of letters is read backwards
the letters sit swallowed up within the single word shoreline

parts.note: the letters ELIN sit inside this word

explanation.surface: A flower on the beach is swallowed by the tide as it ebbs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flower' is the crossword trick for a river, something that flows. The hidden run ELIN in shorELINe, read backwards, gives the African river.
explanation.definitionFit: In crosswords a flower is something that flows, a river, and the Nile is Africa's great river.

clue.text: Student inspired by well-informed, suitable, old mate?

indicators.note: the student is breathed in by the word for well-informed, so goes inside it

parts.note: hep is an old form of hip, meaning in the know
L, for learner, is the usual crossword student, from the L-plate
meet is an archaic word for fitting or suitable

explanation.surface: A learner is enthused by a knowledgeable, proper old friend.
explanation.definitionFit: Helpmeet is an archaic term for a wife or partner, a companion and helper, from the Bible's 'help meet for him'.

clue.text: Casually state times for visit

parts.note: to drop a remark is to mention it casually
by means times, as in four by four

explanation.surface: Someone casually mentions times when they'll come round.
explanation.definitionFit: To drop by is the idiom for calling in on someone informally, paying a short visit.

clue.text: A number of shops mostly providing tea

indicators.note: mostly means most but not all of the word, so its last letter goes

parts.note: a chain is a group of shops under one owner

explanation.surface: Most branches of a retail chain sell tea.
explanation.definitionFit: Chai is the Hindi word for tea, often spiced and milky, now common in English.

clue.text: Big band opening in Hungary, Spain and Ireland when on tour

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter, here of Hungary

parts.note: E is the international vehicle code for Spain, from España

indicators.note: touring moves things around, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A major group starts a European tour through Hungary, Spain and Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when on tour' sends only Ireland on the move; the H and E stay in place at the front.
explanation.definitionFit: A headliner is the main act on a bill, the big-name performer or group topping it.

clue.text: Attendant in home regularly going round with help

indicators.note: the alternate letters surround the word for with
regularly takes every other letter of home, the first and third

parts.note: alternate letters H and M
and means together with
aid is help

explanation.surface: A care worker at home makes rounds offering assistance.
explanation.definitionFit: A handmaid is a female servant or personal attendant, as in a lady's maid.

clue.text: It's normal to be put off a wicked act

indicators.note: put off means disturbed or thrown, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone shrugs that being put off by wrongdoing is quite usual.
explanation.definitionFit: A mortal sin in Catholic teaching is a grave offence against God, a deeply wicked deed.

clue.text: Booster requires filling new can here with nitrogen

indicators.note: the nitrogen fills the rearranged letters, going inside them
new means made afresh, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: N is the chemical symbol for nitrogen

explanation.surface: A fuel additive needs this tin refilled with nitrogen gas.
explanation.definitionFit: An enhancer improves or intensifies something, so it acts as a boost.

clue.text: Soldier guarding back of unit alongside tense, tough instructor

indicators.note: the tense letter sits right next to the rest, after it
the soldier wraps round and protects the letter, putting it inside

parts.note: a marine is a soldier serving with a navy

indicators.note: the back of a word is its last letter, here of unit

parts.note: T is the grammar abbreviation for tense

explanation.surface: A soldier protecting the rear of his unit stands by a stressed, hard drill instructor.
explanation.definitionFit: A martinet is a strict disciplinarian, named after a famously harsh French army drillmaster.

clue.text: Beams put up in an auditorium

indicators.note: an auditorium is where things are heard, so the word is taken as it sounds

parts.note: to put up is to raise

explanation.surface: Stage beams are hoisted in a theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: Rays are beams of light, narrow shafts of radiation.

clue.text: Army leader taking tips from renegades in the slammer?

indicators.note: the army leader takes in the tips, holding them inside

parts.note: CIC is short for C-in-C, commander-in-chief

indicators.note: the tips are the first letters of renegades, in and the

explanation.surface: A general takes advice from deserters locked up in prison.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the slammer' reads as prison, but here it is one who slams, a reviewer who pans things.
explanation.definitionFit: To slam a work is to criticise it harshly, so a reviewer who slams is a slammer.

clue.text: Manual rewritten for graduate

indicators.note: written again in a new form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A handbook gets revised for a recent graduate.
explanation.definitionFit: An alumna is a female former student of a school or university.

clue.text: Clean, flash young boxer?

parts.note: a mo is a moment, a flash
a boxer is a breed of dog, and its young is a pup

explanation.surface: A smart, showy young fighter is spotless.
explanation.definitionFit: To mop up is to wipe clean a spill, clearing up the mess.

clue.text: Dull assignment — it takes 24 hours

parts.note: an assignment is a piece of work
something lasting 24 hours takes a day

explanation.surface: A tedious task that eats up a whole day.
explanation.definitionFit: Workaday means ordinary and unexciting, suited to everyday working life.

clue.text: Bothersome behaviour shown by "characters" in stag group

indicators.note: the letters shown in the phrase stag group give the answer as a run inside it

explanation.surface: A rowdy stag party's antics cause trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: A stag party is a British pre-wedding night out for the groom and friends.
explanation.definitionFit: Aggro is British slang for aggressive, troublesome behaviour, short for aggravation.

clue.text: Sudden camera movements from right to left

indicators.note: reading from right to left runs the word backwards

parts.note: pans are sweeping horizontal camera movements

explanation.surface: A camera jerks abruptly across the scene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sudden camera' looks like a phrase, but 'Sudden' alone is the definition, as in a snap election.
explanation.definitionFit: Snap as an adjective means done on impulse without warning, like a snap decision.

clue.text: TUC agrees fresh end to striking — a good and bad thing

indicators.note: fresh suggests remade anew, so the letters are rearranged
the end of striking is its last letter

explanation.surface: Union leaders agree a new end to industrial action, mixed blessing that it is.
explanation.walkthrough: The TUC is Britain's Trades Union Congress. The answer comes from a Punch cartoon in which a curate, served a bad egg, says parts of it are excellent.
explanation.definitionFit: A curate's egg is an idiom for something with both good and poor parts, a mixed bag.

clue.text: Set about probing source of power cut

indicators.note: the word for about pokes into the others, going inside them
the source of a word is its first letter, here of power

parts.note: pared means trimmed or cut
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: Someone investigates the cause of a blackout.
explanation.definitionFit: Set means ready, as in 'ready, steady, go', so it is a synonym of being prepared.

clue.text: Footballer from France snubbed one of its divisions?

indicators.note: snubbed suggests a snub nose, cut short, so the last letter goes

parts.note: Eric Cantona is the French former Manchester United forward

explanation.surface: A French footballer is cold-shouldered by one of his nation's regions.
explanation.definitionFit: A canton is an administrative subdivision of a French arrondissement, so a division of France.
